question: Should ClawHub continue owning support reports for the externally hosted OpenClaw bootstrap, or should this issue be redirected to the installer-owning repository with explicit legacy-command guidance?
rationale: The failure is credible and user-blocking, but the relevant script and deployment are outside ClawHub, so automation cannot decide the permanent support and issue-routing boundary.

options.title: Route to installer owner
options.body: Keep the setup problem visible, move implementation ownership to the OpenClaw installer repository, and publish the supported bash command for legacy URL users.

options.title: Track cross-repository here
options.body: Keep this issue as the ClawHub tracking item until the external installer is hardened and a macOS/Homebrew run proves the legacy invocation no longer fails.

options.title: Wait for updated proof
options.body: Request current macOS, zsh, Node source/version, and complete redacted installer output before selecting a cross-repository action.

recommendation.title: Route to installer owner
recommendation.body: Keep the setup problem visible, move implementation ownership to the OpenClaw installer repository, and publish the supported bash command for legacy URL users.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent current-main history on ClawHub’s maintained install and package boundary and is the best available router for deciding where the external bootstrap report belongs.
